verdict.rationale: Algolia's own Search API is documented to manage indices and records, which implies record-level writes rather than full reindexes. A community user describes keeping Firebase data synced through a single cloud function, which suggests incremental updates work in practice. However, the evidence never names add, update, or delete operations or says how quickly changes become searchable. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-record add/partial-update/delete operations, any stated indexing latency or near-real-time guarantee, and independent confirmation of how fast changes appear in search.

support.subject: As a developer, document adds, updates, and deletes become searchable in near real time without a full reindex

citations.quote: The Algolia Search API lets you search, configure, and manage your indices and records
After you’ve structured your data into records, choose how to send them to Algolia.
Linking the two took a single Firebase cloud function after importing data with a simple node script.
